newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel oil steady in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel oil steady in quiet trade.

text.p: NWE straight run fuel oil prices steadied on Monday, with sellers not seeing the recovery they hoped for after clearing storage tanks packed with product last week, traders said.
Bids for low sulphur straight-run were barely higher at $101-$102 fob.
Offers were at a notional $106 fob basis or higher, but attracting no attention at that level, with sellers disappointed two large sales last week had not yet boosted interest.
But bidders were reported holding numbers down, aware that cargoes would be available in good quantity by mid-April.
One small cargo was heard sold in mainland Europe to an inland buyer at $105 fob.

Russian material was attracting interest. Two cargoes of E-4 were sold to one buyer on Friday at 3 means +$3.50 and +$4. A small M-40 piece was seen bought on Monday at 2 means plus $7.75 and a larger cargo of M-40, with high water content, was failing to find a buyer at 2 means +$12.
"I think premiums of $5 are a bit overdone," said one trader. "I think they will start to come off in a week or so, reflecting better supply and refinery economics."
In the Mediterranean low sulphur straight-run was looking long, with three cargoes of Libyan material loading over the weekend and a Tunisian tender to be awarded this week.
One of the Libyan cargoes was rumoured already sold but no details were known.
Some traders saw the straight-run starting to weigh on low sulphur cracked values in the first third of April.
